findings.title: Cleanup registers removal of a literal "alias" IDP instead of the created ones
findings.body:
The new test registers its cleanup as `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove`. That targets an IDP whose alias is literally "alias", not the `idp-alias-N` providers just created. The same mistake appears at line 425 for `idp-alias-20`.

The cleanup therefore never removes the 21 IDPs this test creates. They stay in the test realm and can skew later tests that count login IDPs or rely on cache state. Use the actual alias variable when registering the cleanup.

findings.title: Global login predicate semantics changed to exclude non-public org IDPs
findings.body:
`LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` is a public SPI helper. It now also requires org-linked IDPs to have `BROKER_PUBLIC=true`.

This was added to support cache-invalidation decisions, but it silently changes behaviour for every other caller of the predicate. For example, flows that legitimately show an organization's non-public brokers after the user has identified the org would now filter those brokers out.

It also means the predicate disagrees with the `getForLogin` javadoc, which describes eligibility without mentioning publicity. Consider keeping the SPI predicate unchanged and applying the broker-public check locally in the cache invalidation logic.

findings.title: remove() now always performs an extra DB lookup
findings.body:
`remove()` now unconditionally calls `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)`, bypassing the cache. Previously this lookup was only done on the `isInvalid` path, where the cached copy was unusable.

Every IDP removal now issues an additional database query even when a valid cached entry exists. The cached entry could be used to evaluate the login predicate instead.

If `storedIdp` is null on the invalid path, `registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp)` throws an NPE. That behaviour is pre-existing, but this refactor makes it easier to hit.

findings.title: Update invalidation compares org-aware wrapped model against raw model
findings.body:
In `update()`, `idpById` comes from `getById`, which returns the org-aware wrapper. That wrapper's `isEnabled()` also depends on whether the organization (and the org feature) is enabled. The incoming `model` is a plain `IdentityProviderModel`.

When the linked org is disabled, the login predicate gives different results for `original` and `updated` even if the IDP's own fields are unchanged. The login caches are then invalidated needlessly.

For correct comparisons, base the decision on the IDP's stored fields (for example `idpDelegate.getById`) rather than the wrapper.
